title: Relax planner-mode.sh: allow Planner commit/add/branch; keep history-rewriting git blocked; add rollback rule
spec:
Why: user decision 2026-09-17: the Planner may commit, branch and push what it is allowed to write (.orchestrator/**, human-applied guardrail files, dotfiles), and must document every change so it can be rolled back. It still never edits source.

What (4 files, exact):
1. .claude/hooks/planner-mode.sh — in the "git history writes" grep (the line starting `if grep -qE '(^|[;&|[:space:]])git[[:space:]]+`), change the alternation so it blocks ONLY: merge|rebase|cherry-pick|apply|am|reset[[:space:]]+--hard|filter-branch. Remove commit, add, checkout -b, switch -c, stash, restore from it. Keep the optional `-C <dir>` group. Update the comment above it to: "# 1) history rewriting is the merge queue's and the workers' job. commit/add/branch/push are allowed (guardrails.sh still blocks force-push and push to main)." Update the deny() text: replace "The Planner never edits source or commits." with "The Planner never edits source. It may commit, branch and push; every commit message states what and why, and decisions.md gets a dated entry with the revert path." Everything else in the file unchanged.
2. tests/test_orchestrator.py — class PlannerMode.test_bash: move these from `blocked` to `allowed`: "git commit -m x", the git add + heredoc commit case, "git checkout -b memory-skill". Add to `blocked`: "git rebase main", "git reset --hard HEAD~1", "git merge task/T-0001", "git -C ~/dotfiles cherry-pick abc123". Keep the final worker-passthrough assertion. Do not touch other test classes.
3. CLAUDE.md — "## Never" first bullet: change to "- Edit source files. Delegate via `codex` / `codex_reply`; Codex cooling → `executor_fallback(complexity)` → a Claude tier executes. Never do the work yourself. Committing, branching and pushing are allowed." Then under "## Always" append item "11. Rollback record: every commit you make says what and why in its message and gets a dated `decisions.md` entry (skill `memory`, `record.sh add`) naming the revert path: `git revert <sha>`, or the backup file for a human-applied change. Do the work yourself; never hand the human commands to run, except for paths guardrails.sh protects."
4. README.md — in the "## Access model" list, append one bullet: "- The Planner may commit, branch and push but never edits source (`planner-mode.sh`, PreToolUse). Every change carries a rollback path in `decisions.md`."

Then run `.claude/hooks/tests-green.sh` (or `uv run python -m unittest tests/test_orchestrator.py`). Commit on the task branch with message "planner-mode: allow Planner commit/branch/push; block only history rewriting; rollback rule" and a body naming the revert path (`git revert` this commit). Report: summary, `git diff --stat`, failures-only test output.

Done. Final report:

**Summary:** Loosened `planner-mode.sh` so the Planner (fallback executor in this worktree) may `commit`/`add`/`checkout -b`/`switch -c`/`stash`/`restore`/push; it now blocks only history-rewriting commands (`merge`, `rebase`, `cherry-pick`, `apply`, `am`, `reset --hard`, `filter-branch`). Updated deny-message text, `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, and the `PlannerMode.test_bash` test cases to match, per the 2026-09-17 decision that the Planner may write/commit/branch/push but never edit source, with every change carrying a rollback path.

**Files changed:**
```
 .claude/hooks/planner-mode.sh | 6 +++---
 CLAUDE.md                     | 3 ++-
 README.md                     | 1 +
 tests/test_orchestrator.py    | 9 +++++----
 4 files changed, 11 insertions(+), 8 deletions(-)
```

**Test output (failures only):** one pre-existing, out-of-scope failure — `Guardrails.test_edit_protected_path` fails identically with my changes stashed out, because `protected-paths.txt` hardcodes `~/code/orchestrator/.claude/settings.json` while tests run against this worktree's path (`wt/T-0002/.claude/settings.json`), so the prefix never matches. Not in scope (only `PlannerMode` was to be touched), unrelated to this task. All 4 `PlannerMode` tests pass, and the acceptance-criteria pipe checks (`git commit -m x` → 0, `git rebase main` → 2, `git reset --hard HEAD~1` → 2, source `Write` → 2) all verified correct when run outside a `T-xxxx`-named cwd (this worktree's own dirname otherwise short-circuits the hook via the existing scope-guard passthrough rule).
